paths.description: Homepage/popular-listing archetype and first-visit consent journey; primary public discovery surface.
Humor board listing archetype; represents category/board indexes sharing the board template.
Representative popular article/detail page; covers reading content and article chrome.
Search-results journey for “축구”; covers query entry, results, and navigation onward.
Account authentication form; covers labels, focus, autofill, persistence, and modern auth posture.

findings.summary: The public UI is light-only under the user’s dark preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually the same light page as the default capture, and the CSS feature probe found no prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map surfaces/text to light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme palette while preserving contrast.

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Recon found no view-transition CSS and the site uses traditional abrupt MPA navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply cross-document View Transitions to same-origin page changes, with reduced-motion-safe fallbacks.

findings.summary: Long listing and article pages provide static rather than scroll-state-aware navigation.
findings.evidence: Screenshots and CSS inspection show a static dense header and no scroll-state/container-query or progress treatment on long pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or responsive sticky-header state using declarative scroll-state guidance.

findings.summary: Page changes and in-page navigation do not visibly cue where attention moved.
findings.evidence: Representative MPA surfaces switch abruptly and the probe found no highlight, transition, or scroll-marker treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use directional transitions and visible focus/highlight cues after route or state changes.

findings.summary: A first-visit consent interstitial obscures every primary content surface.
findings.evidence: Homepage, article, and search captures show a centered modal plus full-page scrim before any user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a compact, equally clear consent choice that does not block reading where lawful, and keep reject/manage choices as prominent as accept.

findings.summary: The consent experience is implemented as custom role=dialog divs rather than the native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: Recon found four role=dialog DIVs but zero <dialog>, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for the modal consent flow with correct focus restoration and platform dismissal semantics.

findings.summary: Dense global chrome competes with primary community content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile captures show multiple utility rows, a large category bar, ads, controls, and shortcut panels around a narrow content column.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate secondary navigation and utilities into progressive disclosure while retaining direct routes to core boards.

findings.summary: Mobile visitors receive a scaled desktop canvas instead of a responsive layout.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport the layout reports no viewport meta and an inner width of 1050 CSS pixels; screenshots show tiny, zoomed-out desktop UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1, then replace fixed-width layout constraints with fluid intrinsic sizing and responsive regions.

findings.summary: Reusable navigation, list, and form components do not adapt at component level.
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found no @container rules; components retain desktop geometry when embedded in a mobile viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable regions and adapt their internals with size-aware container queries.

findings.summary: Many controls and links are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The accessibility probe counted 151 rendered interactive targets with a dimension below 24px; login controls are as small as 13x13 and 22px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase controls to comfortable touch target sizes, preserve spacing, and keep visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Mobile lab loading misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.4s, FCP 3.7s, Speed Index 4.1s, and TTI 7.1s, despite a faster unthrottled trace.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the redirect and shorten render-blocking/resource chains; prioritise the actual LCP resource.

findings.summary: The critical resource chain is broad and cache policy leaves savings.
findings.evidence: HAR records 16 stylesheets and 20 scripts; Lighthouse estimates 1.28s render-blocking savings and 162KiB cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate/conditionally load styles, defer non-critical scripts, and set useful immutable cache lifetimes for versioned assets.

findings.summary: The homepage ships avoidable unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 151KiB unused JavaScript and 21KiB unused CSS; HAR attributes 826KB transferred to scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by surface and load ad/search/board code only when the relevant feature is needed.

findings.summary: Interactive controls and form fields lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails label, select-name, and iframe-title; probes found icon-only search controls and login fields without robust names in repeated header forms.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate labels with every field, name icon-only controls, and title embedded frames according to purpose.

findings.summary: Text and essential links fail minimum colour contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the color-contrast audit and reports links distinguished only by color.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text/link tokens to WCAG contrast minimums and add non-colour link affordances.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is inconsistent and focus is not consistently visible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails heading order and main-landmark checks; the DOM probe shows repeated H1/H2 sequences, while focused submit controls have outline none and no box shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one logical heading hierarchy and landmark structure; apply a visible :focus-visible treatment to every interactive control.

findings.summary: Text becomes too small to read comfortably on narrow screens.
findings.evidence: The 360px homepage and login captures show the entire 1050px desktop UI scaled to roughly one-third size.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix viewport/reflow first, then use fluid type sizing and comfortable line height/measure for lists, articles, and forms.

findings.summary: The experience fails mobile reflow and target-size expectations.
findings.evidence: No viewport meta is present, the mobile canvas remains 1050px wide, and Lighthouse fails target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable user-scalable responsive viewport behavior, reflow content to 320 CSS pixels, and enlarge targets.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and multiple browser hygiene issues remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports two deprecation warnings, six BFCache failure reasons, Inspector issues, legacy JavaScript, and third-party-cookie usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated calls and BFCache blockers, address DevTools Issues, and stop serving avoidable legacy code.

findings.summary: The page is not mobile-friendly and some links are not crawlable.
findings.evidence: The viewport meta tag is absent and Lighthouse fails crawlable-anchors; robots also blocks most paths for generic crawlers.
findings.suggestedFix: Add responsive viewport metadata, use real descriptive href links, and align crawler rules with intended public reach.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are incomplete and inconsistent across crawlers.
findings.evidence: The canonical URL exists, but /sitemap.xml returns 404; robots permits major routes for selected search bots while blocking most routes for generic and many AI crawlers.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a current sitemap and document a deliberate, consistent crawler policy for public boards and articles.

findings.summary: Public community entities lack structured data coverage.
findings.evidence: Recon found Open Graph metadata but no evidenced JSON-LD entity model for the organization, board, or representative article.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite and Article/DiscussionForumPosting JSON-LD that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Cookie and XSS transport defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS/HSTS/nosniff are present, but CSP is absent; all five observed cookies lack Secure and the auth-like idntm5 cookie lacks HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure, HttpOnly where appropriate, and Lax/Strict SameSite cookies; deploy a nonce/hash CSP in report-only then enforcing mode.

findings.summary: The first load has a large advertising and analytics footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 13 cross-origin hosts and Google ad/analytics trackers; the consent dialog says data may be shared with 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors and data purposes, delay optional requests until informed choice, and batch only necessary analytics.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only with no evidenced phishing-resistant option.
findings.evidence: The login surface exposes user_id/password controls; recon found no WebAuthn/passkey affordance or credential-management flow. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside account recovery, keeping any permission prompts contextual.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors; HSTS max-age is only 3600 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, strict Referrer/Permissions policies, and increase HSTS after deployment validation.

findings.summary: Most rendered content is not present in raw HTML.
findings.evidence: Discoverability comparison found only 24% rendered-token coverage without JavaScript, although the page is not an empty JS shell and title/H1/description survive.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the current listing/article content and keep real links/forms functional before JavaScript enhancement.

findings.summary: The consent decision steers users toward acceptance.
findings.evidence: The blocking first screen gives prominent “agree” and “manage options” actions but no equally direct reject-all action, while describing processing by 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Give accept and reject equivalent prominence, minimise defaults, and make later withdrawal as easy as consent.

findings.summary: Authentication fields have no evidenced native or accessible validation contract.
findings.evidence: Login probes show no required/aria-invalid/error-announcement attributes on user ID or password controls and no visible inline recovery guidance before submission.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required constraints, validate after interaction, attach specific error text with aria-describedby, and announce the summary.

findings.summary: Sign-in inputs omit autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: Both header and dedicated login forms report empty autocomplete values for user_id and password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password, then support passkey conditional UI where available.

findings.summary: The observed account entry flow relies only on a password and does not surface modern reauthentication or recovery assistance.
findings.evidence: The dedicated login surface contains user ID/password and keep-signed-in controls but no passkey or contextual account recovery action beside the form.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey sign-in/reauthentication and keep recovery, persistence, and security implications clear and reversible.

findings.summary: Asset delivery still uses legacy placeholders and lacks responsive source selection.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 14 legacy-format resources and one image without srcset; custom transparent GIF lazy-loading is used instead of native loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive modern image sources and replace transparent-GIF lazy loading with loading=lazy/decoding=async.

findings.summary: Optional advertising and analytics work dominates the initial payload.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 71 cross-origin requests and roughly 1.03MB cross-origin bytes, including ad/analytics scripts before a consent decision.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional vendors and background work until user intent, and conditionally import only the modules needed for the current page.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts are disproportionate for a text-led listing page.
findings.evidence: Scripts account for 826KB of 1.05MB transferred; Google Ads and Tag Manager are among the largest origins while first-party document bytes are small.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors, self-host only justified assets, and defer remaining integrations.

findings.summary: The site exposes public content but no structured agent actions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse marks WebMCP tool/form checks not applicable; source/recon found no registered agent tools, while robots explicitly permits several user-invoked AI agents.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent participation is intended, expose narrowly scoped read/search/post tools with explicit confirmation and safe schemas.

taskList.title: Rebuild mobile viewport and layout behavior for true reflow and touch use
Repair security headers and cookie attributes
Make the consent experience non-blocking, balanced, and privacy-minimising
Fix accessible names, structure, contrast, focus, and target sizing
Reduce render-blocking, unused, and third-party JavaScript
Improve raw-HTML coverage and indexing metadata
Modernise authentication assistance and add passkeys
Add preference-aware theming and restrained navigation cues
Simplify chrome and use semantic native overlay primitives
Modernise image delivery and browser platform hygiene
Evaluate safe structured agent capabilities only if product intent supports them
